basis: Polydactyly is shared across the MKKS phenotypes; retinal, renal and metabolic disease depend on the Bardet-Biedl subtype, and cardiac defects are a minority.
Acute infectious inflammation of the conjunctiva.
ATP synthase deficiency with cardiomyopathy (22/25) and developmental impairment (30/30); myopathy with hypotonia (80-99%) and contractures (30-79%) supports muscle involvement.
Disorder of the adrenal cortex; no additional organ damage is shared across the umbrella.
Skin, hair, nails and teeth define the dysplasia; ptosis and structural eyelid abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
Ocular hypotension with blindness; disease is confined to the eye.
Severe combined immunodeficiency defined by defective T- and B-lymphocyte development; no specific extraimmune organ damage is established as common.
Defined as isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; respiratory distress reflects cardiac failure rather than independent pulmonary disease.
Inherited phosphate-handling disorder defined by hypophosphatemia, nephrolithiasis and osteoporosis.
Absent calvarial bones and scalp define it; HPO reports cerebellar hypoplasia in 80-99% and neuronal migration defects in 30-79%, conflicting with the definition's usually spared CNS.
Disease of hepatic blood vessels; both liver and vascular location define the umbrella.
Severe inherited adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; reproductive abnormalities and transient salt-wasting crises do not establish another organ axis.
Syndrome defined by scalp skin folds and intellectual disability.
Inherited carnosinase deficiency; intellectual disability, seizures and developmental regression are reported in 80-99%.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia in 7/7 annotated patients; individual bone abnormalities occur in 2/7 and do not establish additional involvement.
Skeletal and nail dysplasia with renal disease (CKD 2/2); retinal dystrophy, progressive visual loss and blindness reported in 1/1. Dental defects (2/2) omitted under the cap.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy with peripheral neuropathy; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 5/6 patients. Hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.
Hereditary lymphatic vascular malformation causing lymphedema; no separate common tissue injury is established.
Immune-mediated orbital inflammation affecting extraocular skeletal muscles; ocular location and muscle inflammation define the disease.
Familial synovial cartilage proliferation with severe short stature; joints and skeleton define the disorder.
Aneurysm of the subclavian artery; stroke and limb ischemia are potential complications rather than common defining organ damage.
Contractures, craniosynostosis, cleft palate and intellectual disability define it; congenital urinary tract disease with reflux and hydronephrosis occurs in 1/2 patients.
Hepatic fibrosis, renal dysplasia and intellectual disability define it; ptosis 80-99%, visual impairment/coloboma 30-79%. Hearing and respiratory impairment (30-79%) omitted under cap.
Inflammation of the gallbladder wall; gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis. Infection is not intrinsic to every case.
Immune-mediated lymphoproliferative disease of lymphoid tissue; systemic symptoms and compression do not establish common direct damage to another organ.
